description: The popup panel and its settings page. It reads the in-memory snapshot, reads and writes its own settings, asks for a window that fits its content, listens for two events (core:default already allows that), and hides itself on Esc; it opens no dialogs, runs no shell commands and reaches no network. Commands the application defines itself need no entry here — WP5's set is get_ui_state, set_theme, dismiss_hint, set_panel_height, open_panel, open_settings, get_config, set_config, reset_hint, dismiss_detailed_suggestion, get_autostart, set_autostart and quit, and WP7 adds statusline_status, statusline_preview and statusline_apply — so the list stays the core defaults plus the one window permission the panel uses to hide itself. THE THREE WP7 COMMANDS RUN ANOTHER PROGRAM, AND THAT IS WHY THEY ARE COMMANDS RATHER THAN A SHELL PERMISSION: granting the webview tauri-plugin-shell would let it run anything, while these three run one binary, beside this one, with arguments this application chooses. Resizing goes through set_panel_height rather than core:window:allow-set-size, so the webview cannot resize its window except by asking, and the Rust side clamps what it asks for. THE WP5 PLUGINS ARE NOT LISTED, AND THAT IS THE POINT: tauri-plugin-notification and tauri-plugin-autostart are both driven from Rust — the toast is shown by the refresh loop, and the autostart switch goes through this application's own get_autostart/set_autostart commands, which read the state back from the plugin — so the webview never invokes a plugin command, and granting it notification:default or autostart:default would hand the panel a capability it does not use. The minimal grant for a plugin nobody calls from the front end is no grant at all. Every permission beyond that is listed with the reason it is needed.
